artists.biography: Monster Magnet is an American stoner rock band. Hailing from Red Bank, New Jersey, the group was founded by Dave Wyndorf (vocals and guitar), John McBain (guitar) and Tim Cronin (vocals and drums). The band first went by the names "Dog of Mystery", "Airport 75", "Triple Bad Acid" and "King Fuzz" before finally settling on "Monster Magnet", taken from the name of a 1960s toy made by Wham-O, which Wyndorf liked when he was a child.

perplexity.description:
Powertrip is Monster Magnet's fourth studio album, released on June 16, 1998, marking the band's commercial breakthrough. The record represents a refinement of the New Jersey band's signature sound—a fusion of heavy groove, psychedelia, and punk-inspired aggression drawn from influences like Hawkwind, Black Sabbath, and Funkadelic. While maintaining the cosmic heaviness that defined their earlier work, Powertrip added a polished production sheen that made the material more accessible to mainstream audiences. Songs like "Crop Circle" and "Bummer" exemplify the album's heavy, spacious approach, while tracks such as "19 Witches" lean toward garage-rock sensibilities.

The album's creation was unconventional and deliberate. Frontman Dave Wyndorf spent 21 days outside Las Vegas, writing one song per day while drawing inspiration from the city's nightlife and hip-hop culture's confident swagger. This process resulted in a record that balanced the band's stoner-rock foundations with arena-ready ambition. The title track became a defining moment for the band, achieving their first UK Top 40 hit when released as a single in January 1999. The album itself achieved gold certification within six months of release and remains Monster Magnet's most commercially successful record.

Powertrip stands as the peak of Monster Magnet's mainstream success, charting internationally and topping the US Billboard Heatseekers chart. The album's lead single "Space Lord" became a staple of MTV rotation and has maintained cultural presence through film, television, and video game placements for decades. For many fans, Powertrip remains their favorite Monster Magnet album, solidifying the band's status as significant figures in 1990s rock music.
